mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening household demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and compresses earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 5.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and capital expenditure, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 3% signals a dual shock of higher rates and inflation, which erodes real corporate earnings and increases discount rates, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 3% AND CPIAUCSL > 3% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.6%) in at least 50% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average by more than 10% for two consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and consumer confidence, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month moving average +10% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.4%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is a contradictory signal indicating labor market churning; this ambiguity reduces investor confidence, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises AND UNRATE rises in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.2%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month average by more than 15% for three consecutive months signals elevated precautionary savings, which typically precedes a consumer spending slowdown and ultimately reduces corporate revenues, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month moving average +15% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.
